'''Zak Zaz''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] who worked as a [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] at a [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|hospital]] in the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. When hundreds of [[Sundari Mandalorian school/Legends|Sundari school]] children were taken to the [[Medcenter/Legends|hospital]] where he worked, suffering from some manner of [[Poison/Legends|poisoning]], Zaz was able to correctly diagnose the cause of their illness to be heavy concentrations of the chemical [[Slabin/Legends|slabin]] within [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|the tea]] they had consumed.

==Biography==
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Zak Zaz was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] and a member of the peaceful [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction. Zaz was a trained [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] who worked in [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|one of]] the newly opened [[Medcenter/Legends|hospitals]] in the New Mandalorian [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="Corruption" />

[[File:DrZazDiscovery-Corruption.png|thumb|left|250px|Dr. Zaz discovers that the slabin is the cause of the sickness]]
In the wake of Mandalore's reestablished neutrality,<ref name="DoM">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref> [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade routes]] to Mandalore were closed, forcing the New Mandalorian people to turn to a [[Mandalorian black market conspiracy/Legends|black market network of trade]] in order to obtain the supplies they so desperately needed. From this [[Black market/Legends|black market]] network came a group of [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], who illegally imported cases of [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|Ardees Beverage tea]] to Sundari; these smugglers wished to maximize their [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|profits]] and thus used the chemical [[Slabin/Legends|slabin]] to dilute the [[Tea/Legends|tea]]. However, the Moogans added too high of a slabin concentration to the tea, making it [[Poison/Legends|toxic]] for an unwary consumer. Distributed to [[Sundari Mandalorian school/Legends|Sundari's schools]], the slabin-laced tea soon had hundreds of New Mandalorian school children being taken to Doctor Zaz's hospital seeking treatment for severe [[Stomach/Legends|stomach]] pain as a result of the slabin overdosing.<ref name="Corruption" />

Zaz, seeking an answer to the question of what had caused these children's sudden illness, investigated both the food and drinks served at the children's school but found nothing out of the ordinary. However, the New Mandalorian leader, [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], and the visiting [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|senator]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], acquired a bottle of the affected tea for Zaz to test; his test revealed the presence of the high slabin concentrations, leading the two [[Politics/Legends|politicians]] on their way toward putting an end to the Moogan smuggling ring. Kryze and Amidala also acquired antidotes for the slabin poisoning, which Zaz and the hospital staff administered to the sick children.<ref name="Corruption" />

==Behind the scenes==
Zak Zaz made his first appearance in ''[[Star Wars]]'' in the [[2010]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television episode, "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]]," part of the series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] and during which he was voiced by [[Corey Burton]].<ref name="EpGuide" /> Zaz is the second Mandalorian doctor to be introduced into [[canon]], and the first to be identified among the New Mandalorian faction. The first Mandalorian doctor to appear in ''Star Wars'' was [[Mij Gilamar]], a character originating in the [[Republic Commando|''Republic Commando'' series]] of novels by author [[Karen Traviss]].
